title: AXI4 Legal-Pattern Debugger
description: Open a rule family to decide whether the example is legal, identify the responsible channel owner, and see the assertion or scoreboard state a verifier needs.

signals.name: VALID independence
signals.expansion: Source must not wait for READY
signals.description: LEGAL: a destination may wait for VALID before asserting READY. ILLEGAL: an address or data source waits for READY before asserting its VALID, because mutually waiting endpoints can deadlock.
signals.direction: VALID is source-driven; READY is destination-driven on each channel
signals.sampled: A transfer occurs on a rising ACLK edge with both VALID and READY HIGH
signals.verificationNote: Assert that once VALID rises it remains asserted, with a stable payload, until a handshake. Liveness analysis must separately examine READY policies.

signals.name: B response
signals.expansion: Accepted AW plus accepted final W
signals.description: In AXI4, a slave can assert BVALID only after it has accepted the write address and accepted the final write-data transfer with WLAST asserted.
signals.direction: BVALID/BRESP are slave-driven; BREADY is master-driven
signals.sampled: Dependencies are established by AW and final W handshakes, not by signal assertion alone
signals.verificationNote: Track AW acceptance and final-W acceptance independently, then allow exactly one B response for the transaction.

signals.name: Burst bounds
signals.expansion: Length, size, wrap, and 4 KB checks
signals.description: A burst is illegal if a transfer is wider than either interface, a WRAP length is not 2/4/8/16, a WRAP start is not size-aligned, or any byte crosses a 4 KB boundary.
signals.direction: AxADDR, AxLEN, AxSIZE, and AxBURST are master-driven on AW or AR
signals.sampled: The complete burst contract is captured by the address-channel handshake
signals.verificationNote: Compute every derived beat address and active byte range from the accepted controls; do not check only the start address.

signals.name: LAST count
signals.description: WLAST and RLAST identify the final transfer declared by AxLEN. A write source may deassert all WSTRB bits on unwanted remaining beats, but it must still complete the declared number of transfers.
signals.direction: WLAST is master-driven; RLAST is slave-driven
signals.sampled: LAST matters on an accepted data transfer where VALID and READY are HIGH
signals.verificationNote: Count accepted beats rather than clock cycles, because backpressure can hold one beat for multiple cycles.

signals.name: ID ordering
signals.expansion: Order is scoped by transaction ID
signals.description: Responses for transactions in the same required ordering domain must remain ordered. Different IDs can permit out-of-order completion, subject to the rest of the AXI ordering rules and target capabilities.
signals.direction: Request IDs are master-driven; BID and RID are returned with responses
signals.sampled: Allocate on an address handshake and retire on the matching B or final R handshake
values: Different IDs: reordering can be legal
signals.verificationNote: Maintain per-ID queues and never use address alone as the response key.

signals.name: Read after write
signals.description: The independent read and write channels do not, by themselves, guarantee that a write response appears before data for a later read. The master and system ordering mechanism must establish any required dependency.
signals.direction: The dependency spans independent AW/W/B and AR/R channel flows
signals.sampled: Use accepted transactions and architectural completion rules, not issue order alone
signals.verificationNote: A scoreboard must model the intended memory-ordering policy instead of inventing a universal cross-channel response order.
